pages.x: By 1860 four million people were enslaved in the southern states, and the country was split over whether slavery could spread west. When Abraham Lincoln, who opposed its spread, was elected president without a single southern state, South Carolina left the Union. Ten more slave states followed and formed the Confederate States of America.

On 12 April 1861 Confederate cannon opened fire on Fort Sumter, a Union fort in Charleston harbour. It surrendered the next day. Both sides expected a short war, and in July crowds came out from Washington with picnics to watch the first big battle, at Bull Run. They fled in panic with the beaten Union army.

pages.t: The Battle Hymn of the Republic
pages.x: Union soldiers marched to a camp song about John Brown, an abolitionist hanged in 1859 for trying to start a slave revolt. In 1861 Julia Ward Howe heard it on a visit to the army and wrote new words to it that night. Her Battle Hymn of the Republic, printed in 1862, became the anthem of the Union cause.

pages.x: At first Lincoln fought to save the Union, not to end slavery. But enslaved people fled to the Union lines by the thousands, and the war changed. On 1 January 1863 his Emancipation Proclamation declared the enslaved in the rebel states free, and let Black men join the army. By the end some 180,000 had served.

Harriet Tubman, who had escaped slavery and led others to freedom on the Underground Railroad, served the Union army as a scout and spy. In June 1863 she guided gunboats up the Combahee River in South Carolina, in a raid that freed more than 700 enslaved people. No other woman led an armed raid in the war.

In July 1863 General Robert E. Lee invaded the North and met the Union army at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. In three days some 50,000 men were killed, wounded or missing. Lee's last great charge failed and he retreated. The next day, far away on the Mississippi, the Confederate city of Vicksburg surrendered to Ulysses Grant.

In November Lincoln spoke at the new cemetery for the dead of Gettysburg. His speech took about two minutes. In 272 words he said that the dead had given their lives so that the nation might have a new birth of freedom, and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.

In 1864 Grant fought Lee in Virginia week after week, whatever the losses, while General William Sherman burned Atlanta and marched to the sea at Savannah, wrecking farms and railways to break the South's will. No other war has killed so many Americans.

pages.x: In April 1865 Richmond fell, and Lee surrendered his army to Grant at Appomattox Court House. Grant let the Confederates keep their horses for the spring ploughing. Five days later Lincoln was shot at a theatre in Washington by an actor who supported the South, and died the next morning.

The Union was saved and slavery ended: the 13th Amendment abolished it in December 1865, and later amendments made those who had been enslaved citizens, equal in law. But after a few years the South brought in segregation and kept most Black people from voting, and the fight for those rights went on for another century.

Four million enslaved people were freed
